REGIME CALL: neutral, held from prior cycle (not upgraded to risk-on). Rationale -- (1) the wire tape shows the Hormuz conflict intensifying, not cooling, tonight: fresh US strikes on Iranian territory, a disabled tanker, Iran refusing talks, and Brent/VIX both ticking back up rather than continuing yesterday's pullback; (2) against that, PSX itself has now rallied hard for two straight sessions (+1.02% Tue, +~1.6% intraday today), a genuine local buy-the-dip signal that domestic investors are pricing the shock as contained, but a two-session equity rally against a still-escalating wire is a divergence to respect, not yet a green light; (3) desk georisk score ticked UP to 59 moderate from 55, conflict factor maxed -- the radar agrees the backdrop has not cleared; (4) domestic anchors remain solidly constructive and unchanged: SBP on hold, CPI easing, IMF program on track, reserves stable and rising, sub-policy-rate T-bill yields, orderly fiscal financing. Net: domestic conditions alone would support a risk-on tilt, but the external/geo overlay (maxed conflict stress, active strikes, no negotiation track, next fuel-price hike likely) is not yet clean enough to upgrade past neutral. Normal setup limits apply; energy-cost-sensitive import/consumer sectors still warrant caution pending an actual stand-down of the blockade.
